newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc to rise, trade mulls copper backwardation.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc to rise, trade mulls copper backwardation.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices were likely to rise again on Tuesday after surging to 6-3/4 year highs overnight while the trade closely watched the sharp rise in copper's backwardation, dealers said.
"Zinc is definitely overbought. It needs a correction, but I don't think it will come until later in the week," a senior dealer for a metal trading company in Singapore said.

"The close above $1,500, with the technical indicators trending high, suggests further gains to $1,530. Failure to do so could spark off a corrective move, as we look to place initial stops below $1,490," Rudolf Wolff said in its daily
But a Japanese trader said zinc, which rose on Monday to hit an intra-day peak of US$1,502 on the LME, should fall. "I think $1,500 is ripe for some profit-taking," he said.
At 0230 GMT, the trade quoted three-month zinc at around $1,498/503 a tonne against the late quote on the LME of $1,500.

The sharp rise in zinc prices prompted China to ship thousands of tonnes of the metal to warehouses in Singapore. The volume of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 36,575 tonnes on Monday against 12,700 tonnes in early May.
Some 5,000 tonnes of zinc remained off-warrant and China is said to be shipping another 2,000 tonnes of zinc to Singapore. Some traders, however, said the total could be up to 10,000 tonnes.
Premiums for 25-kg zinc ingots eased further and were being quoted at a year-low of $0-$5 a tonne, traders said.
"It's now zero to five dollars. What can you do? There's just too much zinc here," a dealer said.

Asian copper trading, however, has slowed sharply after the backwardation in London shot up on the back of aggressive third Wednesday pricing yesterday. The backwardation in the region was quoted at $250 against $240/$260 on the LME.
"The market's movement this afternoon will depend on the backwardation," a dealer said.
"It's difficult to tell how copper will behave today, but it should drop a bit since people may want to make money with prices at these levels," another trader said.
Rudolf Wolff, however, said that with the red metal's "positive close, the upside is expected to remain pressurised whilst keeping a close eye on the spread."
Three-month copper was seen by Asian dealers at around $2,314/319 a tonne, little changed from the last quote on the LME of $2,315/320 a tonne on Monday.
Aluminium premiums in Singapore continued to hover at high levels as available supplies remained scarce. Premiums for western aluminium 20-25 kg ingots were steady at $80-$100 a tonne.
The volume of aluminium in the LME's Singapore warehouse was at 6,500 tonnes, down 125 tonnes from last Friday and the 15,825 tonnes reported at the end of April.
